transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (AuroraHead Partnerships), Sofia Gomez (Aurora PM), Ethan Li (Aurora Cloud Architect)

Summary/Context:
Short sync to map out technical requirements for getting Redwood listed in the AuroraCloud marketplace, confirm reference architecture patterns (VPC, private deployment, gateway/routing), and align on security checklist and deliverables for an internal preview listing.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'll kick off — we've got Liam with me, SE, and then Raj, Sofia, Ethan on the Aurora side. Quick agenda: listing checklist, ref arch, security, next steps.
[00:18] Raj Patel: Thanks Maya, yeah really excited to get Redwood in the marketplace. Sofia's leading the product side, Ethan on infra. We have a few partners in flight so trying to standardize the pattern.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Great, quick intro from me. I'll focus on the technical ref arch and what we need from Aurora for the private/VPC variant — things like subnet ranges, NAT/IGW patterns, and KMS integration.
[00:45] Sofia Gomez: Our marketplace requires a listing preview and reference architecture diagram plus an integration repo link and sample deployment. We also surface security artifacts during review (SOC2, pen tests).
[01:05] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll share a checklist after this call. Quick question — Aurora, are you planning to host Redwood as a managed marketplace offering (we run infra) or list a bring-your-own-license template?
[01:20] Ethan Li: We're targeting the managed listing first — customers click in Aurora marketplace and we spin up a managed Redwood instance inside their VPC or on a dedicated tenant. We also want a BYOL option later.
[01:34] Liam O'Connor: Okay that maps to two reference patterns: 1) Managed (Redwood hosts but connects into customer VPC via peering or private link), 2) Private deployment (Redwood software deployed into customer VPC/on-prem). We'll prepare both diagrams.
[01:50] Raj Patel: What's your expected SLA for the managed option? We typically need RTO/RPO and latency SLOs to show.
[02:02] Maya Chen: For managed hosted offering, we publish latency profiles per model; typical SLO is 99th percentile < 300ms for short completion workloads, but we'll include examples and the Dedicated product for higher throughput/guarantees. We'll provide the performance profiles and an SLA attachment to the listing.
[02:25] Sofia Gomez: Good, also need to document quotas, pricing tiers, and any burst/overage mechanisms.
[02:32] Maya Chen: We'll include that. Liam, can you walk through the ref arch?
[02:37] Liam O'Connor: Sure. Starting with the managed option: we recommend a private endpoint or VPC peering so traffic doesn't traverse public internet. For high security customers we support private control plane with customer-managed networking — that ties into KMS for key management. Typical flow: customer API requests go to Aurora gateway -> private connectivity to Redwood control plane -> inference routed to dedicated GPU pools or multi-tenant runtime.
[03:05] Ethan Li: For the private control plane, how do you handle model versioning and rollouts? We need to know if we can pin model versions per customer.
[03:14] Liam O'Connor: Yes — model pinning, canary rollouts, A/B testing, automatic fallback. We'll document the rollout process and how it maps to Aurora's deployment lifecycle. There may be small variances in kernel selection for different GPU types but functionally the features are the same.
[03:33] Raj Patel: Are there known integrational gotchas with Aurora's native LB or gateway? We use the term "Aurora Edge Gateway" and there are some header stripping behaviors.
[03:44] Ethan Li: Right, we do have an L7 proxy that strips some headers by default, but we can configure path-based routing and pass through custom headers for auth tokens. We'll share config snippets.
[03:56] Sofia Gomez: On the listing front, we need a short 50-100 word description, logos (SVG/PNG), a 1-page reference architecture PDF, and a link to a demo or trial.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Got it. I'll put together the copy. Quick note — our branding team prefers the SVG, will attach.
[04:20] [crosstalk] Raj Patel: Also can you provide an estimated cost per seat or per throughput tier? Customers ask that a lot.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: We can provide a cost matrix: token-based pricing for hosted API, and reserved-capacity pricing for Dedicated. I'll draft an example cost table for the listing. It's an estimate — final pricing will depend on committed capacity.
[04:47] Sofia Gomez: Security — we need SOC2, ISO, encryption at rest/in transit details, RBAC, audit logs, and whether you support SSO via SAML/OIDC.
[04:59] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SSO SAML and OIDC, RBAC, tenant-level audit logs, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. We'll attach SOC2 report and an FAQ doc.
[05:15] Ethan Li: For KMS — do you support external HSM or bring-your-own-KMS? We have customers that insist on HSM-backed keys.
[05:24] Liam O'Connor: We support KMS/HSM integrations via standard connectors; for private/on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs over a secure channel. We'll note the supported providers in the security doc.
[05:36] Raj Patel: Any requirement on data residency? Some Aurora customers require data to remain in-region.
[05:43] Maya Chen: Yes — we support regionally pinned deployments and can ensure inference and logs remain in-region. We'll document the region mapping for Redwood-hosted clusters.
[05:55] Sofia Gomez: Great. Back to the ref arch: can you produce a diagram that shows networking, auth flow, where metrics/tracing live? Our reviewers like to see telemetry flows.
[06:06] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely — I'll include traces for per-request observability (we emit tracing hooks compatible with OpenTelemetry and we expose per-route latency/cost dashboards). The diagram will show the control plane, data plane, KV cache, and where caching reduces token cost.
[06:25] Maya Chen: Quick interjection — Raj, what is Aurora's timeline for getting a preview listing into the partner portal?
[06:32] Raj Patel: If we have draft assets in two weeks and security docs in hand, we can queue a preview for the internal marketplace by mid-August. Official public listing would be September after final approvals.
[06:45] Ethan Li: For the managed setup, we need the exact healthcheck endpoints and any expected TLS configs.
[06:53] Liam O'Connor: We'll share endpoints: /health, /v1/infer (or /v1/chat) and certificate rotation expectations; and note that when using privateLink we can use mutual TLS.
[07:06] [00:07:06] Sofia Gomez: On the joint solution collateral — we want a 1-page partner solution brief and a how-to deploy guide. Can Redwood provide a sample Terraform/ARM template for the private deployment?
[07:17] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll provide sample Terraform for onboarding into Aurora's marketplace flow and for private deployment (minimal infra). Liam, can we commit to a Terraform sample?
[07:25] Liam O'Connor: Yes — I'll produce a starter Terraform repo with variables for VPC, subnets, KMS keys, and model pins. We'll host the repo link in the listing.
[07:35] Raj Patel: Does Redwood do automated benchmarks? We sometimes run perf checks before we approve listings.
[07:41] Liam O'Connor: We have benchmark harnesses. If Aurora wants, we can run a short benchmark in a staging account or provide sample perf profiles. For Dedicated use-cases we can run capacity planning tests.
[07:54] Ethan Li: We'll want to validate a tail-latency profile, especially for multi-tenant vs dedicated.
[08:02] Maya Chen: We'll include both multi-tenant and Dedicated profiles.
[08:07] [pause, background noise]
[08:20] Sofia Gomez: A few compliance questions: how are logs retained and can we surface audit logs to a customer's SIEM?
[08:27] Liam O'Connor: Audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed to customer SIEMs via forwarders. Retention is configurable; for marketplace listings we'll document defaults and options.
[08:40] Raj Patel: On credentials — do you expect Aurora to provision API keys on behalf of the customer or will customers register directly with Redwood?
[08:50] Maya Chen: For managed marketplace we typically provision app-level credentials that live in the Aurora tenant; for private deployments customers manage keys. We'll outline both flows in the listing.
[09:03] Ethan Li: Regarding contract terms, do you require a long-term commit to Dedicated, or can customers try managed and then move to Dedicated later?
[09:12] Maya Chen: Customers can start with hosted managed and then convert to Dedicated with a migration plan. We'll include a migration playbook.
[09:20] Sofia Gomez: Any IP or data sharing constraints for the listing? We need language for our legal team.
[09:27] Maya Chen: We'll provide standardized partner terms and a data processing addendum. I'll have our legal contact share the DPA and sample MSA.
[09:36] [00:09:36] Raj Patel: Great. Let's map owners and timing then.
[09:41] Maya Chen: Owners: Maya sends listing copy + logo + deck (due 8/6), Liam sends ref arch + Terraform starter + perf profiles (due 8/11), Ethan sends VPC diagrams + security questionnaire (due 8/7), Sofia confirms portal access and approvals (due 8/9).
[09:58] Sofia Gomez: Also please flag any blocked items so we can escalate internally — legal signoff or infra changes especially.
[10:05] Liam O'Connor: Noted. One technical caveat: for some GPU kernels in Aurora's older instance types we might see slightly higher latency; we'll call that out in the perf doc to avoid surprises.
[10:18] Raj Patel: Competitors: a few partners already integrated (GeneralCloudAI, EdgeServe); we should call out differentiation points in listing.
[10:27] Maya Chen: We'll call out production-first SLOs, transparent cost controls and the Dedicated/reserved capacity offering as differentiators.
[10:36] Sofia Gomez: Demo/trial — can you provide a demo account or a short recorded walkthrough to include in the listing?
[10:44] Maya Chen: Yes, Liam will record a 5-7 minute walk-through video and we'll attach demo creds for internal preview.
[10:51] Liam O'Connor: I'll do the recording by next week.
[10:55] [some typing sounds]
[11:05] Ethan Li: For marketplace billing integration — Aurora handles customer billing; we need to confirm how usage metrics get relayed so Aurora can bill customers.
[11:15] Maya Chen: We can push usage reports and per-customer aggregated token counts to Aurora via a secure reporting API or S3 drop. We'll include a sample schema.
[11:28] Raj Patel: Great. Anything else?
[11:31] Sofia Gomez: Quick question on the listing lifecycle — after internal preview, what's the typical review time?
[11:36] Raj Patel: Usually 2 weeks for internal review if all artifacts are present; security/legal may add time. Public listing typically 3-4 weeks from preview depending on approvals.
[11:47] Maya Chen: Okay, sounds reasonable. We'll hit the deliverables.
[11:52] [wrap-up] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya sends copy + deck (8/6), Liam ref arch + Terraform + perf (8/11), Ethan VPC + security (8/7), Sofia confirms portal access (8/9). Follow-up RA review week of 2026-08-10.
[12:08] Raj Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll unblock portal access and look for the docs.
[12:12] Ethan Li: I'll send the VPC and security doc.
[12:17] Sofia Gomez: We'll get approvals moving.
[12:20] Maya Chen: Thanks all.

Shared artifacts mentioned during call:
- Redwood partner preview deck (link will be shared)
- Sample Terraform repo (Redwood) - to be shared in follow-up
- Security questionnaire (Aurora internal doc link - Ethan to share)
- Performance profiles spreadsheet (Redwood)

End of transcript.

Recap & next steps (from call):
- Redwood to provide listing copy, logos, preview deck, and demo video.
- Redwood SE to provide ref arch diagram, Terraform starter, perf profiles.
- Aurora to share VPC topology, security questionnaire, and enable dev portal preview.
- Follow-up reference architecture review scheduled for week of 2026-08-10.
